title: Creator tests dead internet theory using viral AI influencers with unexpected results
key_facts: The 'dead internet theory' says most of the internet is bots; a 2016 Imperva report claimed bots were 52% of web traffic on 100,000 sampled domains.
AI influencers such as Jean Philanthrope have taken off on Instagram, TikTok and X.
X user @notdwd ran 'Project Jeffy' from 5 Oct to copy that success using ChatGPT prompts and swapped-in viral video formats.
Their character Lil Jean had three followers from five posts, the best reel reaching 288 views.
A second character, Jeffy, also flopped: two videos got four likes and 170 views on TikTok by 8 Oct.
UNILAD concludes humans can be relieved that the internet is 'not dead yet'.
quote_evidence: Starting on October 5, they created a Philanthrope-esque character called Lil Jean.
At the time of writing, Lil Jean only has three followers from five posts, with the most successful reel only getting 288 views.
why_it_matters_hint: A small test suggests copying viral AI influencers is not easy, but it is one anecdote.
notes: Single anecdotal experiment by one X user; events before 9 Oct.
